newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Mineral Commodities says gold at White Foil.
newsitem.headline: Mineral Commodities says gold at White Foil.

text.p: Mineral Commodities NL said on Tuesday that drilling at the White Foil joint venture near Kalgoorlie, Western Australia, operated by French mining group Cogema, had indicated the presence of a major gold deposit.

"These results give us great deal of confidence that we have found a major deposit," Mineral Commodities chairman Peter Topham said in a statement. "The extension of depth is exciting and suggest we have the makings of a substantial resource."
Intercepts included 20 metres at 3.93 grammes per tonne (g/t), four metres at 12.89 g/t, six metres at 7.6 g/t and five metres at 5.96 g/t, the company said.
Mineral Commodities holds 49 percent of the prospect.
Mines and Resources (Australia) Pty Ltd, a unit of French the state-owned Cogema mining group, holds the remainder and is operator of the project, 20 km west of Kalgoorlie.
Topham said the Latest drilling results indicated a substantial gold resource over a 1.4 km strike length.
Reverse circulation drilling has so far been completed over a 1,140 metre length on a 40 metre by 20 metre basis, he said.
"Results from this drilling will be used to compile an ore reserve later this year," he said.
Step-out drilling had also outlined significant intersections including 40 metres at 3.98 g/t.

"A significant amount of work has been done on the project since the discovery hole in November, more than 300 reverse circulation holes have been drilled for approximately 35,000 metres and eight diamond holes for more than 1,000 metres," Topham said.
The exploration expenditure since discovery has been of the order of A$2.4 million, he added.
"We are planning to spend another similar amount before the end of the year," he said.
Mineral Commodities shares closed a cent lower at 58 cents. The stock has traded between 32 cents and 70.8 cents this year.
